title: Role activation cadence and SIEM sampling guidelines
content:
Purpose:
Quick working doc to capture a concrete operational cadence for privileged role activations and a practical SIEM sampling strategy that balances evidence fidelity vs. ingest cost across Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployments. This is intentionally pragmatic (checklists + config examples) rather than a policy-only doc.

Scope:
- Applies to all tenant and infra roles that permit elevated access (admin, ops, billing-admin, tenant-owner, deployer).
- Covers activation cadence (how long roles are active), re-certification windows, emergency bypass, and automated evidence capture.
- Covers SIEM export sampling rules and example queries per hosting tier (hosted, dedicated, private).

Assumptions / constraints: 
- Hosted environment has centralized SIEM with budgeted ingest; Dedicated customers may have higher retention SLAs; Private customers often push events to customer-managed SIEMs with varying capacity.
- RBAC v2 is in active rollout; this doc is tied to that rollout (see linked confluence).

Terminology (short):
- Activation: a time-bound enablement of a role (JIT - just-in-time).
- BAA: Break-glass / emergency activation.
- Evidence package: log + context artifacts required for audit (auth event, session metadata, triggered actions, request IDs, linked PR/issue).

High-level recommendations (one-liners):
- Default to JIT activations for all privileged roles; default TTL = 4 hours for interactive sessions, 1 hour for sensitive ops like key rotation.
- Require multi-factor re-affirmation on re-activation if within 24 hours of last activation for same role+principal.
- Record a minimum evidence package per activation (see checklist).
- Use adaptive SIEM sampling: sample less for noisy, high-volume non-actionable events; full capture for activation, privilege-change, and sensitive data-access events.

Activation cadence matrix (suggested defaults):
- role: infra-admin; default-ttl: 4h; re-cert-window: 90d; jitauth: mfa + sso; allow-reauth-within-24h: yes; break-glass: manual ticket + 4-eyes review post-factum.
- role: deployer; default-ttl: 2h; re-cert-window: 60d; jitauth: sso; allow-reauth-within-24h: yes; break-glass: limited to infra-admin escalation.
- role: tenant-support; default-ttl: 1h; re-cert-window: 30d; jitauth: sso + audit-annotation required.
- role: key-rotator; default-ttl: 1h; re-cert-window: 30d; jitauth: sso + hardware-backed key vault claim; allow-reauth-within-24h: no.

Note: TTLs above are starting points; product/business teams can tighten for specific customers or regulatory regimes.

Evidence package checklist (minimum):
- auth_event_id (uuid)
- principal_id (user/service account) + group membership snapshot at time-of-activation
- role_name + activation_ttl (seconds)
- auth_method (SSO, MFA type, session_token)
- source_ip, region, device_fingerprint (if available)
- session_start_ts, session_end_ts (or null if open)
- list of high-level actions performed while role active (action_type, resource, request_id)
- linked_ticket_or_change_id (if any)
- export_hash (sha256) of the evidence package for immutability checks
- post-activation reviewer_id + review_ts (for break-glass or elevated activations)

Automation tasks (evidence):
- On activation event: assemble evidence package, store to immutable S3 bucket (or customer endpoint in Private), emit SIEM event type: RBAC_ACTIVATION with payload refs.
- On privileged action: annotate action logs with activation_event_id to tie actions to the activation window.
- Scheduled job (daily): verify evidence packages have required fields; raise alerts for missing critical fields.

SIEM sampling & export guidelines (practical):
Principle: always export 100% of RBAC_ACTIVATION, RBAC_DEACTIVATION, PRIVILEGE_CHANGE, KEY_ROTATION, and SENSITIVE_DATA_ACCESS events. For other event classes (AUTH_ATTEMPT, TOKEN_REFRESH, HEARTBEAT), apply sampling by volume and hosting tier.

Sampling table (recommended):
- Hosted (central): RBAC_ACTIVATION=100%, PRIVILEGE_CHANGE=100%, SENSITIVE_DATA_ACCESS=100%, AUTH_ATTEMPT=10% baseline + 100% for failures, HEARTBEAT=1% aggregated.
- Dedicated (customer-dedicated infra): RBAC_ACTIVATION=100%, PRIVILEGE_CHANGE=100%, SENSITIVE_DATA_ACCESS=100%, AUTH_ATTEMPT=25% baseline + 100% failures, HEARTBEAT=2% aggregated.
- Private (customer-managed SIEM): advise 100% export for activation & sensitive events; provide an export contract template and recommended sampling config (customer may override).

Sampling implementation notes: 
- Sampling must be event-type aware and deterministic per principal to avoid losing correlated traces. Use hash(principal_id + day) modulo N to sample.
- For high-volume agents (ingest pipeline traffic, automated telemetry) use aggregated counters (per-minute rollups) instead of full event export.
- Ensure sampled events still include activation_event_id when applicable so audits can reconstruct sessions.

SIEM export field recommendations (flat schema to encourage cross-SIEM compatibility):
- event_id (uuid)
- event_ts (ISO8601)
- event_type (RBAC_ACTIVATION | RBAC_DEACTIVATION | PRIV_CHANGE | SENSITIVE_DATA_ACCESS | AUTH_ATTEMPT)
- principal_id
- principal_type (user | svc )
- role_name
- activation_id (optional, links to evidence package)
- resource (ARN-like string)
- action (string)
- result (success | failure)
- host_tier (hosted | dedicated | private)
- tenant_id (if applicable)
- request_id (trace id)
- sampling_reason (sampled | full | aggregated)

Retention & cost guidance (per hosting tier):
- Hosted: keep full evidence packages for 90 days online, 1 year cold; SIEM export sampling reduces ingest for non-critical events.
- Dedicated: default to customer SLA; recommend 1 year online if contract allows, otherwise 90 days + archive to cold.
- Private: support customer-defined retention; provide recommended defaults and a template for export contracts describing minimum guaranteed fields.

Operational playbook (short runbook):
1) Activation alerting: trigger if activation without matching ticket for roles requiring change control.
2) Missing-evidence alert: daily job flags evidence packages missing required fields.
3) Post-facto reviews: weekly sample of break-glass activations for manual audit.
4) SIEM drift check: monthly verify that exported schemas match expected fields; rotate sampling thresholds if ingest patterns change.

Example SIEM queries (high-level pseudo-SQL/KQL):
- Find activations with no linked_ticket: SELECT event_id, principal_id, role_name, event_ts FROM events WHERE event_type = 'RBAC_ACTIVATION' AND linked_ticket IS NULL AND event_ts > now()-30d
- Reconstruct session: SELECT * FROM events WHERE activation_id = '<uuid>' ORDER BY event_ts
- Sampled auth failures trend (hosted): SELECT count(*) by day FROM events WHERE event_type='AUTH_ATTEMPT' AND result='failure' AND sampling_reason!='aggregated'

Implementation snippets (examples):
- Deterministic sampling pseudo: if (hash(principal_id + date) % 100) < sampling_pct then export_event(full_payload) else emit_aggregated_counter()
- Evidence export cron (example): 0 * * * * /opt/redwood/bin/evidence-flush --pending --verify-fields || alert("evidence-flush-failed")

Customer-specific notes:
- For Dedicated customers with strict compliance, escalate to 100% export for auth_attempts and token_refresh.
- For Private deployments, include a small helper daemon that can push full evidence packages to customer SIEM endpoint; include validation on handshake for schema compatibility.

Open questions / items for follow-up:
- Do we standardize re-certification windows by role sensitivity level (e.g., S1,S2,S3)? (P0: Product + Security decision)
- How do we instrument device_fingerprint consistently across mobile/web/cli clients? (Req: telemetry input from devexp/dev)
- For archived evidence packages, define immutability & retention handling for e-discovery requests (Legal).

To-do (owners):
- Arjun: prototype deterministic sampler and add unit tests (due 2025-10-10)
- Lena: update confluence RBAC v2 rollout page with TTL defaults (due 2025-09-30)
- Derrick: draft Dedicated export contract appendix with recommended retention and ingest rates (due 2025-10-07)
- Maya: coordinate with Legal on e-discovery retention language (due 2025-10-14)

Appendix: short example activation log (JSON text blob for engineers):
{
  "event_id": "a1b2c3d4-...",
  "event_ts": "2025-09-15T21:14:22Z",
  "event_type": "RBAC_ACTIVATION",
  "principal_id": "user:maya.h",
  "role_name": "infra-admin",
  "activation_id": "act-20250915-0001",
  "activation_ttl_s": "14400",
  "auth_method": "sso+mfa",
  "host_tier": "hosted"
}

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep sampling logic simple at first; prefer deterministic over random to make audits reproducible.
- Don't ship heavy device fingerprinting without privacy review.

Revision history:
- 2025-09-15 Maya H: initial draft

End.
